summary: Aérodrome de Belle Île (BIC/LFEA) is a small island airport serving Belle-Île-en-Mer, the largest of the Breton islands off the coast of Brittany in northwestern France. Located in the commune of Bangor, it provides a vital air link for visitors and residents traveling to this scenic Atlantic island, which is otherwise primarily reached by ferry from Quiberon. The airport primarily handles small regional aircraft and charter flights, with its dramatic coastal setting offering passengers immediate views of the island's rugged cliffs and turquoise waters upon arrival.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Aérodrome de Belle Île?
A: The airport is mainly served by small regional carriers and charter flights, with seasonal service typically connecting to mainland cities like Nantes and Lorient.

Q: How long is the flight from the French mainland to Belle-Île?
A: Flights from the mainland generally take around 30-40 minutes depending on the departure city.

Q: Are there car rental services at the airport?
A: Limited car and bicycle rental options are available at or near the airport, though booking in advance is recommended, especially during the summer season.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: The airport operates year-round but with reduced schedules outside the peak tourist season from June to September.
transport_tips: Pre-book taxi transfers from the airport to your accommodation, as public transport on Belle-Île is infrequent and rental cars are limited. Renting a car or scooter upon arrival is the most practical way to explore the island, as bus services connect only the main towns. If traveling off-season, arrange return transport well in advance as ferry and flight schedules are reduced.
local_tip: Request a seat on the right side of the aircraft when flying in from the mainland—the approach over the Aiguilles de Port-Coton and the island's dramatic southern cliffs is considered one of the most scenic landings in Brittany.
